notes.meaning: Paul and his helpers work alongside God, and they plead gently with the Corinthians. "God's grace" here means God's kind offer to make peace with us through Christ. To receive it "in vain" is to hear it and gain nothing from it, for example by going on living in sin as if nothing had changed.

differ.view: A person can truly receive grace by faith and still lose its benefit. It is not in vain if they go on in holy living to the end.
The warning calls church members to search their hearts and make sure their faith is real, not self-deceived. It also calls ministers to keep urging people, so the offer is not made for nothing.

notes.meaning: Paul quotes Isaiah 49:8, where God promises to hear and help His chosen Servant, the Messiah. Paul says that time has now come with Christ. Today God is ready to show mercy. We should not put it off, because tomorrow is not promised to us.

Paul took care not to do anything that would make people trip over the gospel or turn away from it. He knew that one minister's bad conduct brings shame on the whole work of Christ. So he tried to live in a way that gave critics nothing to blame.

Paul shows he is a true servant of God by his deeds, not by bragging. First comes patient endurance. Then he lists three groups of hardships: troubles in general, attacks from people (beatings, prison, riots), and hardships he took on for the work (hard labor, sleepless nights, going without food). He bore them all patiently.

Next Paul names the good qualities his ministry lived by. They are a pure life, true spiritual knowledge, patience, kindness, the work of the Holy Spirit, and real love. He also spoke God's truth and relied on God's power. His only "weapons" were right and holy living, which guarded him on every side, the right hand and the left.

Some people honored the apostles and others insulted them, and they kept going either way. They were called frauds, nobodies, and men close to death. Yet they were true, well known to God and the churches, and still alive by God's care. They had sorrows but always rejoiced. They were poor but made many rich with the riches of Christ. They owned nothing in this world, yet in Christ they had everything.
Paul speaks warmly and openly to the Corinthians. His heart is full of love for them, and so his words pour out freely. He hides nothing from them.

There is plenty of room for the Corinthians in Paul's heart. The problem is on their side, because their love toward him has grown cold and narrow. This may be because of false teachers and quarrels among them.

Paul speaks like a father to his children. The only payment he asks for all his love and hard work is that they love him back in the same way. He wants them to open their hearts to him as he has opened his to them.

The picture comes from the Old Testament law, which said not to plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together. Believers should not tie themselves to unbelievers in ways that pull them toward sin, such as marriage, close friendships, or sharing in idol worship. Light and darkness, and right and wrong, simply do not belong together. We still live and work among unbelievers. We just must not join them in what is sinful.

"Belial" means "worthlessness" and is used here as a name for Satan. Christ and Satan are complete opposites. In the same way, a believer and an unbeliever have nothing in common when it comes to faith and worship.

An idol in God's temple would be a terrible insult to God. Christians themselves are now God's temple, because God lives among His people by His Spirit. Paul gathers Old Testament promises that God will live and walk among His people. He will be their God, and they will be His people.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars think Paul is drawing here on a collected list of Old Testament proof texts, joining several passages into one.

notes.meaning: These words come from Isaiah 52:11, where God called His people to leave Babylon and its idols behind. Paul applies them to Christians. We should keep ourselves apart from sin and false worship and not let anything unclean touch our lives. God promises to welcome those who do this into His own family.

God promises to be a loving Father to His people. They will be His sons and daughters. The Almighty, who rules over all, makes this promise, so it is sure. This great honor should make believers long to live clean and holy lives.
